channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Error correction route preset. Today's ranked reading list collects five relevance-3 skims at the application and tooling edge of quantum computing: 2611.08151 on an ML surrogate for hybrid quantum Monte Carlo, 2611.08220 on differential testing for quantum software stacks, 2611.09873 on trajectory-dependent decoherence and leakage in shuttled multi-spin qubits, 2611.09659 on an OpenQASM3-to-QuEST compiler and HPC-quantum offload model, and 2611.09779 on differentiable digital twins for calibration and characterization of neutral-atom and trapped-ion systems; together they inform workflow acceleration, compiler validation, scaling theory, HPC integration, and calibration methodology, though none directly addresses operation or benchmarking of the current static 16-qubit spin-qubit QPU. item.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
item.description:
Skim theory — Parallel shuttling minimizes decoherence and leakage at short shuttling distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms it over long distances across 2-, 3-, and 4-spin encodings; multi-spin fidelity loss and leakage decompose analytically into sums of at most seven pairwise spin error parameters ϵjkP.

Grade 0.491 · 3.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum error correction with silicon spin qubits” · Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, David P. DiVincenzo, Viatcheslav V. Dobrovitski

Figure

Average fidelity loss 1−FXO of a 3-spin exchange-only qubit versus dimensionless shuttling length λ for sequential, parallel, and triangular protocols across channel separations δ=0.3,0.6,0.8. Parallel shuttling yields lower error at short range, whereas sequential shuttling wins at long range.

Asks

How do spatial and temporal correlations in magnetic noise affect dephasing and leakage during the shuttling of multi-spin logical qubits across different trajectories?

But

Pure dephasing via rotating-frame secular Hamiltonian (neglecting x,y noise and spin relaxation). Neglects inter-spin exchange interaction during shuttling. Assumes stationary, isotropic Gaussian noise field.

Tools

Gaussian random field model of spatio-temporal 1/f noise · mixed-unitary dephasing quantum channel · pairwise dephasing factor expansion · Pauli transfer matrix analysis

Abstract

Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated 1/f noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.

arxave:action.title: Use pairwise dephasing factors to screen shuttling upgrade options

item.arxave:action: If the 24-month upgrade adds shuttling, measure the pairwise dephasing factors for candidate dot geometries and plug them into the paper's fidelity and leakage expressions to compare parallel versus sequential transport before committing to an architecture.

arxave:action.title: Ask authors for parameter regimes relevant to a 16+ dot array

item.arxave:action: Request guidance on which device parameters (noise correlation length, dot spacing, shuttling distance) set the crossover between parallel and sequential shuttling, so the result can be mapped to our upgrade plan.
